scope: targeted primary-literature verification of the surviving phyllary and stickiness mechanism models; no new environmental predictor search and no transport of external effect sizes into East-Asian Cirsium

close_cardueae_analog.result: naturally occurring spines deterred illegitimate Lepidoptera; legitimate bee/fly visitation frequency did not increase after spine removal, although visit duration increased about 20%; spine removal reduced the percentage of filled seeds by 22%
close_cardueae_analog.interpretation: supports antagonist-exclusion benefit with a possible pollinator-handling cost; weakens a simple pollinator-access-primary model
close_cardueae_analog.homology_boundary: Centaurea involucral spines are a closer Cardueae structural analog than Pedicularis cupulate bracts, but they are not identical to authority-coded Cirsium phyllary posture

independent_bract_analog.design: experimental drainage of rainwater-retaining cupulate bracts
independent_bract_analog.result: legitimate pollinators and nectar robbers did not discriminate treatments; seed predation increased after drainage in five of six populations and final seed set declined
independent_bract_analog.interpretation: independently supports protective architecture operating through antagonist exclusion rather than pollinator visitation gain

direct_genus_context_dependence.design: experimental occlusion of sticky bracteal exudates in two Cirsium species

results.Cirsium discolor_Illinois_1980: seed predation was significantly greater when sticky bracteal exudates were experimentally occluded
results.Cirsium flodmani_Minnesota_1980_1982: no experimental treatment effect was evident

direct_genus_context_dependence.interpretation: benefit versus null occurs within Cirsium itself, directly rejecting a universal sign and supporting lineage/site/context dependence

later_direct_Cirsium_null.design: neutralization of sticky inflorescence exudates across later observations/experiments
later_direct_Cirsium_null.result: neutralizing stickiness did not increase seed predators, did not decrease predatory arthropods, and did not decrease successful seed production
later_direct_Cirsium_null.interpretation: the same species can fail to show the earlier defensive effect under other years/conditions, strengthening a context-dependent rather than constitutive defence model

arthropod_mechanism_boundary.result: pollinators did not contact the sticky traps; several seed predators successfully avoided them; ants and aphids were deterred and some predatory arthropods used the inflorescences
arthropod_mechanism_boundary.interpretation: stickiness is guild-selective rather than a general physical barrier, providing a plausible mechanism for sign changes across enemy communities

benefit_context_outside_Cirsium.result: washing sticky flowers increased florivory and lowered fruit set; fruit-set effect varied with population/context
benefit_context_outside_Cirsium.interpretation: contradicts a universal cost model and independently supports context-dependent floral defence

cost_context.design: glandular sticky versus nonglandular morphs under herbivore and exclusion/common-garden conditions
cost_context.result: sticky plants showed large reproductive or demographic costs, including about 45% fewer viable seeds without herbivores in the initial study and 46-60% lower first-year seed production with an overall finite-rate-of-increase penalty in a later field experiment
cost_context.interpretation: supports a resistance-cost term and contradicts universal net benefit

chapter2_use: Trait-specific cause-space reduction: phyllary is narrowed toward protective antagonist-exclusion architecture; stickiness now has direct within-genus evidence for context dependence, making an antagonist-defence versus trait-cost selection mosaic the strongest surviving general explanation. These remain mechanism-level priors and falsified universal rules, not East-Asian adaptation claims.
